Proliferate

proh-LIF-uh-rayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To proliferate to increase rapidly in number.

Online rumors about the store's closure proliferated within hours of the first post.

Worked Example

Cheap knockoff versions of the toy proliferated across marketplaces almost as soon as the original went viral.

This wasn't a slow trickle -- countless copies appeared everywhere almost at once, which is exactly proliferate.

How Proliferate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

multiply

multiply: increase greatly in number

spread

spread: become distributed or reach more people or places

Antonyms

diminish

diminish: become or make smaller in number or amount

How Strong Is It? — increase → proliferate → explode

increase vs. proliferate

increase vs. proliferate: Increasing simply means growing larger, at any pace; proliferating specifically means multiplying rapidly in number.

explode vs. proliferate

explode vs. proliferate: Proliferate describes a sustained, rapid multiplication; explode implies an even more sudden, dramatic burst of growth.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — proli

root — proli: offspring (Latin (proles))

root — fer

root — fer: to bear, carry (Latin (ferre))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make or perform an action (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Proliferate comes from Latin proles ('offspring') + ferre ('to bear, carry') -- literally 'to bear offspring,' extended to mean multiplying rapidly in general.

Use the root in a new word: transfer

Use the root in a new word: transfer: The same ferre root gives us transfer (trans- 'across' + ferre, 'to carry across') and refer (re- 'back' + ferre, 'to carry back').
